_comment: The DEFAULT backend origins compiled into every customer-shipped Vizora Display
build.
SCOPE: these are build-time defaults, i.e. what DEFAULT_CONFIG is seeded with —
not a guarantee about where a running device ends up pointed. src/main.ts applies
URL parameters and stored Preferences over them at startup, and the guarded
update_config path can move a paired device to another host in the same
registrable domain. What this file fixes is BUILD PROVENANCE: which origins a
given artifact was compiled against, which used to depend on the build machine.
COMMITTED ON PURPOSE. These are public values — they ship inside an APK that is
handed to customers, so there is nothing here to protect by hiding. Hiding them is
what created the problem this file exists to fix: until 1.3.13 the production
origins came from a gitignored, machine-local `.env`, with vite.config.ts falling
back to *a different environment* (api.vizora.io) when it was absent. Two people
could build the same commit, with the same signing key, and ship APKs pointing at
different backends — and every release gate would pass, because package id,
version, certificate and artifact hash are all indifferent to which origins a
build was compiled with. See Trivenidigital/vizora-tv#18.
This file is the single source of truth. vite.config.ts compiles these values into
release builds directly and REFUSES to build when an environment variable disagrees
with them, so a developer's local .env can no longer reach a shipped artifact.
Changing an origin here changes the DEFAULT origins compiled into every future
release. It is a release-gating change: the publish-side verifier reads the origins
back out of the packaged APK and compares them against the pin recorded in the
Vizora repo's deploy/tv/release.json. Update both, or publication fails closed.
Moving environments also needs an approved originTransition in that same file — the
published record of what customers are running is never edited just to clear a gate.
